newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco calls for restraint in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Morocco calls for restraint in Iraq.

text.p: Morocco on Tuesday called on the United States and Iraq to avoid any escalation of the crisis in northern Iraq following the U.S. missile attack.
A foreign ministry spokesman said Rabat called for the two parties to "avoid any escalation likely to return instability to the region."

The spokesman said Morocco hoped that all the parties involved would show their restraint "to preserve the territorial integrity of Iraq, peace in the region and the security of its states, in conformity with international resolutions."
Early on Tuesday the United States pounded Iraq with 27 cruise missiles in retaliation for its capture of a rebel Kurdish city. Iraqi President Saddam Hussein vowed to fight back.
Morocco allied itself with the U.S.-led coalition in the 1991 Gulf war which drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait after a seven-month occupation.
